Subject: New supplier setup request — Bluehaven Electronics

Hi Jordan,

Hope you’re well. We are onboarding Bluehaven Electronics as a supplier for spare parts and short-run assembly services. Can you please set up a vendor record for us so your procurement team can issue POs?

Attached is a short supplier overview (company background, NAICS, initial contact details). Quick answers that would help you create the record:
- Bill-to / remit-to: Bluehaven Electronics, 418 Harbor St., Suite 200, San Diego, CA 92101
- Remit contact: Lydia Park, ap@bluehaven.com, +1 (619) 555-0124
- Preferred payment: ACH (US-based bank)
- Tax status: US corporation; EIN available upon request
- Banking instructions will be provided on the ACH enrollment form

Can you confirm what documents you need and your estimated time-to-PO once the record is created? We’re aiming to be on Redwood’s approved supplier list by June for a pilot order.

Thanks,
Sarah Mendez
Procurement Manager
Bluehaven Electronics

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New supplier setup request — Bluehaven Electronics

Hi Sarah — great to hear from you, and welcome. I’ve looped in Laura (Finance/AP) and Karthik (Procurement ops) so we can collect the right artifacts and get the vendor record created.

To complete the vendor master we will need the following items from Bluehaven:
1) Legal entity name exactly as registered (W-9 name if US entity)
2) Federal Tax ID / EIN (or W-8 if non-US)
3) Legal entity type (Corporation / LLC / Partnership) and state of formation
4) Remittance address (mailing and remit if different)
5) Remit contact name, email, phone
6) ACH enrollment or bank details (routing + account or voided check) — we prefer ACH for US suppliers
7) Copy of a W-9 (or W-8) and a copy of a certificate of insurance if you will invoice for services > $10k
8) Copy of corporate formation docs or a corporate resolution if the bank account is held under a different DBA

Next steps from our side: once we receive the completed W-9 and ACH enrollment forms we’ll open the vendor record in our AP system. Typical internal SLA for new vendors is 3–5 business days for creation; POs can be issued after a brief risk/tax review (usually within 5 business days from record creation). If you need faster turnaround for the pilot order, flag the PO as urgent and Laura can triage.

I’m attaching our vendor_onboarding_packet (forms + instructions) and a DocuSign link for the ACH enrollment to make things easier.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Jordan — please see my notes below (forwarding Sarah’s original).

Internal AP checklist / risk items:
- Require completed W-9 and signed ACH enrollment before vendor is payable.
- Validate EIN against IRS TIN matching where possible. If the EIN is missing, request immediately — do not create a record without it.
- For first-year spend > $50k, procurement needs a PO with a signed SOW; require COI (certificate of insurance) at minimum $1M GL if performing on-site work.
- Tax withholding: if we cannot validate the EIN before first payment, place payment on hold and escalate to tax.
- Payment terms: standard Net 30, exceptions only with finance approval. If vendor requests Net 15 for pilot, escalate to me with a business justification.

AP routing: created vendor record goes to AP queue (ap@redwood.com). For urgent pilot PO, Karthik can create a non-catalog PO and mark it as expedited.

Let me know if you want me to own vendor creation once they return the forms — I can do it to speed things up.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Manager, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
